mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT engine typically costs between £1,500 and £2,500, including supply and fit. Rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty. Main dealers often charge significantly more for the same service. Used engines are a popular budget alternative, starting from around £300.

mainEntity.name: Does the Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT have the wet belt problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, the Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT (engine code XYJE) is a traditional, naturally aspirated Duratec engine. It uses a standard dry timing belt, not a "wet belt" running in oil. It is completely free from the catastrophic oil starvation issues associated with the 1.0 EcoBoost. This makes it one of the most reliable choices in the Mk8 Fiesta range.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value and overall condition. For most Mk8 1.1 Ti-VCT models valued under £5,000, a full rebuilt engine replacement is rarely financially viable. A low-mileage used engine or targeted component repair is almost always the most cost-effective solution.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT engine swap typically takes 5 to 7 working days. This includes sourcing the correct XYJE engine code, nationwide delivery to your chosen specialist, and physical installation, fluid top-up, and road testing.

mainEntity.name: What trim levels use the XYJE 1.1 Ti-VCT engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The XYJE 1.1 Ti-VCT engine was fitted exclusively to the base and mid-range trim levels of the Ford Fiesta Mk8 (2017-2019). Compatible trims include Style, Zetec, and Titanium. Higher performance trims (like ST-Line or ST) utilised the 1.0 EcoBoost or 1.5 EcoBoost engines.

historyTimeline.h2: Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Mk8 Ford Fiesta launched in 2017, the 1.1 Ti-VCT (also known as the 1.1 Duratec) was introduced as a naturally aspirated, highly reliable alternative to the turbocharged 1.0 EcoBoost, specifically targeting budget-conscious and city-driving owners.

milestones.description: XYJE (86 PS / 63 kW) introduced in the Ford Fiesta Mk8, offering a robust, traditional timing belt-driven naturally aspirated petrol engine.
Production of the 1.1 Ti-VCT was discontinued as Ford shifted the entire Fiesta range to the updated 1.0 EcoBoost (now featuring a more reliable timing chain design) and mild-hybrid variants.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT is widely regarded as one of the most robust and straightforward engines in the Mk8 lineup. Unlike the 1.0 EcoBoost, it does not suffer from wet belt degradation. However, age-related wear on peripheral components like the ignition system can occur. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Ignition Coil Pack Failure & Standard Wear - Why the Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT Misfires
problems.rootCause: Breakdown of insulation inside the coil pack due to heat and age, leading to misfires, rough idling, and occasional check engine lights.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the faulty ignition coil pack and spark plugs.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended at first sign of misfire; extends engine life significantly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Only recommended if the engine block is cracked or has suffered catastrophic external damage (rare).

If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: For the Ford Fiesta 1.1 Ti-VCT, a full engine replacement is rarely necessary unless the vehicle has suffered catastrophic external damage or severe oil starvation. Targeted repairs (like a coil pack swap) or sourcing a low-mileage used engine are almost always the most sensible and cost-effective routes for this highly durable unit.
